sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. The petitioner in this writ application prays for the following reliefs:
"It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to :
 (i) Admit the Writ petition,
 (ii) Issue notice to the opposite parties and call for  relevant records/documents,
(iii) Issue appropriate writ(s), order(s), direction(s) to quash the notice dated 02.12.2025 in L.A. Case No.24/2021 issued by OP No.3.
(iv) And direct the OP No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner for the land and structure acquisition in Plot No. 499 for the NH 23 Road project."
3.

Mr. Pani, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that being aggrieved by the award passed under section 3-G of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for brevity, 'the Act') and the notice issued by the Competent Authority for Land Acquisition, Talcher, Angul (for brevity 'CALA'), Opposite Party No.3, the petitioner made an objection on 10.12.2025 under Annexure-4.

entities.text: Competent Authority for Land Acquisition, Talcher, Angul
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further submitted that CALA is sitting over the matter and is not referring the same to the competent Principal Civil Court having jurisdiction.
Hence, being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed this Writ Application.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that vide notice dated 02.12.2025 under Annexure-3 issued under Section 3-H(2) of the Act, the CALA had issued notice to one Susanta Samal to receive compensation, who is not a recorded tenant and if the compensation is released in his favour, the petitioner will suffer immensely.
He, therefore, prays for a direction to CALA, Talcher, Opposite Party No.3 for referring the matter to the competent Principal Civil Court having jurisdiction forthwith.

4. Taking into consideration the nature of grievance made by the petitioner in the present Writ Application and that the application under section 3-H (4) of the Act is still pending with the CALA,
Talcher in the district of Angul, this Court directs him to refer the matter to the competent Principal Civil Court having jurisdiction forthwith.

It is, however, made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merit of the objection made by the petitioner under Annexure-4.
5.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, the Writ Application is disposed of.
6. With the disposal of the main Writ Application, the pending I.A. also stands disposed of accordingly.
